metadata.summary: Bounded neutral text records with explicit absence and normal stop/start persistence.

semantics.description: Put replaces one key; get returns found false and empty value only for observed absence, never failure. Maximum32 records. A completed put survives normal stop/start of the service with the same operator-owned data directory. No crash durability, transactions, backup, migration or hostile-code confinement guarantee. See SEMANTICS.md.

evidence.conformance: conformance.json; docs/phase5.0/evidence/native-slice5.log SHA256 3f6ce56bed00172b14910186b4b5e6a7774df67857dc1933f724840b59c9720c;35/35 actual publicHost/SDK/native tests plus separately installed author and crash/restart proof. Local signed-shell/operator-owned-native boundary, trustVerified=false.

proposal.abstraction: Bounded opaque text key/value put/get with explicit found flag, fixed reference quota and normal restart persistence. No search, embeddings, backup, schema migration or product-specific memory API.
proposal.alternatives: Do not add stateful semantics to echo; no MemoryV4 dependency or generic storage engine; explicit native service-owned resource rather than modifying frozen Kernel.
proposal.compatibility: New experimental proposal only; no original definitions/snapshots changed. Admission and separate snapshot require independent parent review and existing Catalog transition.
consumers: Unchanged public SDK record consumer in service-foundation/reference/services.mjs
proposal.existingInsufficient: Echo is explicitly side-effect-free; agent execution and decision evaluation do not offer record persistence. Repurposing any frozen capability would violate its semantics.
proposal.genericRationale: Opaque bounded records demonstrate state ownership and persistence without encoding future products or implementation technology.
proposal.problem: Phase5.0 requires a tiny stateful reference whose completed writes survive normal service stop/start and whose absence is not confused with failure.
providers: Native single-file reference resource (implemented, qualification pending)
Independent external-author file resource (planned; same contract and no product dependency)
proposal.scopes: Application/session; operation grants put/get, neutral permission label example.records. No new grant or scope type.
proposal.security: Existing Host grants enforce capability operations. Native resource ownership belongs to operator topology; no filesystem confinement claim. Permission metadata grants nothing; data never included in diagnostics.

evidence.reference: Owner-authorized Phase5.0 execution of existing local namespace-maintainer workflow. parent.review.json is exact distinct-parent design review, not Owner Acceptance or independently signed identity.

review.rationale: Reviewed actual generated DEV descriptor, definition, namespace policy and proposal with hashes matching the submitted packet; read normative SEMANTICS.md, implementation file-records.mjs, preparation source and frozen Catalog REVIEW.md. Abstraction: bounded opaque put/get with explicit absent-versus-empty, justified stateful reference need; frozen side-effect-free echo is insufficient. Security: existing capability grants, no authority from metadata, native operator-owned resource and explicit absence of sandbox/crash-durability/backup claims; actual Host enforcement remains to be tested. Scopes: existing application/session and operation-grant semantics, no new scope authority. Compatibility: new URI/identity, no modification of existing definitions or release snapshots. This accepts proposal need/design only, not passing implementation, Catalog experimental transition, technical phase completion or Owner Acceptance. Passing implementation/conformance evidence and existing maintainer transition remain required. Preserve cancellation/no-rollback distinction and actual error normalization in conformance evidence; startup corrupt-state failures must remain failures, not successful absence.
review.reviewer: Hermes parent technical reviewer (distinct review session from implementation worker; not Project Owner acceptance)
